first-key-short: The original glossy key is retained. The older gallery showed another design beside it; this comparison uses the same pixels and a source-derived palette.
first-key-specific: Keep its bright highlight and silhouette. Palette compliance does not justify replacing it with a flatter design.
first-key-pro: The returned key keeps its own lighting. The alternative Pro candidate is a separate art choice.
first-robot-short: Preserve this outline and sharp pixel treatment; another robot design is not a conversion.
first-robot-specific: This source already fit its original export without RGB changes. The previous side-by-side used a different robot.
first-background-short: The earlier export already changed zero RGB pixels. Its apparent loss of beauty came from showing a different background beside it.
first-ui-minimal: A source-derived palette preserves the strong light/dark edge more effectively than the unrelated actor palette used in the first pass.
rpg-hero: The larger native canvas permits a full body and readable equipment. Check isometric foot anchors before mixing with other characters.
rpg-golem: Explicit full-body proportions avoid the earlier head-only result. Review feet and animation anchors before requesting motion.
rpg-monster: Readable armored beetle silhouette. Do not assume a single still establishes facing or a usable walk cycle.
rpg-floor: Prompt mismatch: this is a raised diamond block, not the requested flat floor. Keep as an experiment; do not label it a seamless floor tile.
gothic-ui: Source-derived reduction keeps dark recesses, silver bevels and the violet accent. This is a frame illustration, not a validated nine-slice panel.
hex-atlas: Independent hex terrain variants, not a connected transition set. Transparent corners are explicitly composited onto black in the opaque background export. Hardware still stores square 8×8 tiles.
rpg-meadow-tileset: Connected 16×16 grass/path terrain with original adjacency metadata retained. Check repeated seams and corner combinations in a map; a sheet alone cannot certify them.
sci-fi-rover: Native wide canvas gives the vehicle room without shrinking a square design. Review wheel contact and direction before animation.
sci-fi-monster: A separate creature example using the sci-fi palette. No style is prescribed for other games.
city-farm: Color budget is preserved, but the output is angled rather than strictly orthographic top-down. Resolve that projection mismatch before assembling a city.
